coupling.rationale: Layering is disciplined: resolvers → view models → input-bound components, with HTTP, caching and URL knowledge sequestered in one service. Only small tangles: PokeApi leaking into the card component, the ability-specific hidden flag on the shared card type, and TypeResource declared twice (page-data.ts:66, catalog.service.ts:24).

app/src/app/move-table.component.ts:57 — sortable table encapsulates its own sort state per method-table, stretchable to new columns via the columns computed

app/src/app/move.page.ts:82 — but the detail-page shell (title effect, not-found fallback, count/panel styles) is copy-pasted across move/ability/type pages, so a new Items page means duplicating it a fourth time

abstraction_design.rationale: The two real sources of variation in the app (card lists, move tables) are abstracted well, but page shells and the resolver monolith mean similar-but-different features extend by copy-paste rather than by reuse.

findings.issue: All six pages' resolvers, resource interfaces and view models live in one 406-line file; every feature add/remove/removal edits this shared file.
findings.suggestion: Split per feature (e.g. pages/pokemon/{resolver,types}.ts) or colocate each resolver with its page component, keeping only the shared resource interfaces in a common module.

findings.issue: No tests exist in app/ (testLoc 0) even though vitest/@angular/build are wired via `ng test`, so future edits have no safety net beyond the repo-level acceptance tests.
findings.suggestion: Add unit tests for the pure logic that carries the risk: pokemonRefsToCards, humanize/dexNumber/idFromUrl, and the move-table sort comparator.

findings.issue: Document-title logic (`<name> – Pokédex`) is duplicated as an effect in four components (move, ability, type, pokemon) plus static titles in routes.
findings.suggestion: Use a route-level title resolver (route `title: TitleResolver`) or a small shared helper so the suffix format changes in one place.

findings.issue: The `.count` (and panel-adjacent) styles are duplicated verbatim in move.page.ts, ability.page.ts and type.page.ts inline styles.
findings.suggestion: Move the shared detail-page styles (count, facts) into a shared stylesheet or a small presentational component.

findings.issue: pokemonRefsToCards always sets `types: []` while home cards get real types from the catalog, so 'show types everywhere' would require a new catalog index plus edits to the helper and home page — two divergent card paths.
findings.suggestion: Expose a speciesId → types map on Catalog and populate card types in pokemonRefsToCards, converging on one card-construction path.

findings.issue: Sprite URL patterns are split across layers: the card front sprite in the component and the official artwork in page-data.ts:252, both built from hardcoded path strings over PokeApi.media().
findings.suggestion: Centralize sprite/artwork URL construction in PokeApi (e.g. frontSprite(id), artwork(id)) so the media path conventions live with the rest of API knowledge.

findings.issue: TypeResource is declared twice with different shapes (page-data.ts:66 and catalog.service.ts:24), so a change to the type resource's fields needs two edits.
findings.suggestion: Declare the resource interfaces once in a shared api-types module imported by both.

findings.issue: PokemonCardData.hidden exists solely for ability pages, and the `extra` callback in pokemonRefsToCards is a one-off clever extension point; the shared card model is shaped by one caller.
findings.suggestion: Keep PokemonCardData purely presentational and let the ability resolver attach page-specific annotations separately (e.g. a map passed to the component), or accept the flag but document it as page-generic.

findings.issue: @angular/forms is a declared dependency but nothing imports it — dead weight that misleads readers about the app's form strategy (controls are hand-rolled in home.page.ts/pokemon.page.html).
findings.suggestion: Remove the dependency, or use it where the native search/select/filter controls are hand-wired.

findings.issue: Hydration gating is done with non-obvious hacks: `(submit)="$event.preventDefault()"`, `[attr.readonly]` until afterNextRender, and a one-way `value="{{ q() }}"` interpolation on a controlled-by-hand input.
findings.suggestion: Extract the hydration-gate into a tiny directive (e.g. appUntilHydrated) and comment why, so future filter controls follow the pattern instead of rediscovering it.

summary: This is a disciplined, idiomatic Angular 22 codebase: signals and input-bound view models throughout, HTTP/caching/URL knowledge sequestered in one service, and the app's two genuine sources of variation (card lists, sortable move tables) abstracted into reusable components. The main editability tax is the page-data.ts monolith that holds every feature's resolver and view model, plus copy-pasted page shells (title effect, not-found fallback, count styles), which makes per-feature work a shared-file edit and future sibling features (e.g. Items) a copy-paste exercise. Bugs in the core data paths still land in one obvious place, which keeps day-to-day changeability high.

Adding a TTL or LRU means changing the module-level responseCache map in one clearly documented spot.
